> What terrain would make a thermally moving particle spend most of its time near the center, while still occasionally wandering far away?

This post will build the correspondence

\[
\pi(\theta)=\frac{e^{-U(\theta)}}{Z}
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
U(\theta)=-\log \pi(\theta)+C.
\]

The repository preserves the detailed writing and implementation brief in `planning/POST_01_PLAN.md`.

## Relative probability becomes an energy difference

Suppose \(f(\theta)\) is a positive, possibly unnormalized weight. Define

\[
U(\theta)=-\log f(\theta).
\]

Then

\[
U(\theta_2)-U(\theta_1)
=
-\log\frac{f(\theta_2)}{f(\theta_1)}.
\]

```{julia}
#| label: discrete-energy-levels
#| echo: true

using BayesThroughPhysics

weights = [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0]
probabilities, logZ = normalize_logweights(log.(weights))

(; weights, probabilities, logZ)
```

## The Gaussian becomes a spring

For a Gaussian density,

\[
U(\theta)=\frac{(\theta-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}+C.
\]

Ignoring the irrelevant constant, this is a quadratic potential well: the energy of an ideal spring.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-gaussian-energy
#| fig-cap: "A Gaussian density and its quadratic energy landscape."
#| echo: true

using CairoMakie

grid = collect(range(-5.0, 5.0; length=1_001))
energy = grid .^ 2 ./ 2
density, _ = density_from_energy(grid, energy)

figure = Figure(size=(900, 650))
probability_axis = Axis(figure[1, 1]; xlabel="θ", ylabel="density")
energy_axis = Axis(figure[2, 1]; xlabel="θ", ylabel="U(θ)")
lines!(probability_axis, grid, density; color=:teal, linewidth=3)
lines!(energy_axis, grid, energy; color=:navy, linewidth=3)
figure
```

## Coming next

Bayesian models naturally arrive factorized. The prior and likelihood multiply as probabilities, so they add as energies. In the Gaussian case, that addition can be built literally—with springs.
